Subject: Capacity-sizing proposal for Aurora contract — compute slab rightsizing & latency buckets

Simon —

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I’m putting an initial sizing proposal in email so we have something concrete to iterate on. High-level ask from Aurora: 100M tokens/day sustained with spikes up to 20M tokens/hour, model family: llama-3-like 70B (quantized float16/INT8), target p95 generation latency <= 600ms for a 1024-token prompt+response SLO in the US region.

What we recommend (first pass):
- Working throughput estimate: 900 tokens/sec average across the fleet (conservative for expected prompt mix).
- Burst capacity target: support 2.5x sustained for short windows (~30–60m) without violating p95 SLA via burst slabs and routing fallback.
- Headroom: design for ~1.6x operational headroom above forecast sustained TPS to cover load variability and cold-starts.

Karthik — can you validate the tokens/sec math below and give a slab count recommendation tied to common GPU SKUs (A100-80GB, H100-80GB)? Also include a quick ops play for KV-cache warmup and prefix caching assumptions.

Attached: aurora_capacity_model.xlsx (workbook with token-flow tabs), burst-runbook.md (ops playbook). I’ll share the SLA draft once we align on numbers.

Next step: we aim to lock sizing and put a committed reserved slab quote in the term sheet. Simon and Maya, if this aligns with your expectations I’ll prep the comms for procurement + legal.

Best,
Ben

Ben / Laura —

I ran a quick model using the attached workbook. Key assumptions and results:

Assumptions:
- Model perf: 70B quantized — median throughput ~1,200 tokens/sec on H100-80GB for single-request steady-state; p95 latency at this throughput is ~420ms per 1024-token generation when batching is low (1–4). We pad for variance.
- Typical request= 300 prompt tokens + 120 response tokens = 420 tokens average per request; this maps to ~2.86 requests/sec at 1,200 tps.
- Effective sustained tokens/sec requirement for 100M tokens/day = ~1,157 tokens/sec (100,000,000 / 86400). We recommend designing around 1,200 tps sustained to avoid underprovisioning.

Sizing recommendations (US region):
- Baseline reserved pool: 8 H100-80GB slabs (slab = 8x H100 nodes in our infra definition) -> effective sustained capacity ~9,600 tps (with conservative multi-tenant derate applied). This covers locked committed traffic plus 1.6x headroom for daily variance.
- Burst pool (on-demand / reserved-burst): additional 4 H100 slabs available for short spikes (up to 2.5x sustained) with pre-warmed KV-cache strategy.
- Fallback: provide a smaller 30B quantized variant on the dedicated fleet and route 20% of heavy tail requests to it if p95 would otherwise exceed 900ms. This preserves user experience while keeping unit cost lower.

Latency mapping:
- With 8 baseline slabs: expected p50 ~220ms, p95 ~540ms for 1024-token profiles (given prefix caching for common prompts).
- With burst slabs online (total 12 slabs): p95 expected to drop to ~380–420ms across the fleet under short spikes.

Operational notes:
- KV-cache warmup: pre-warm of top-1k prefixes via scheduled warmup jobs reduces cold-start tail by ~120–160ms for affected requests.
- Autoscale policy: scale-up to burst pool should be triggered on 10-min moving average of sustained tokens/sec crossing 1.8x baseline for >5 minutes. Scale-down: 30–60 minute cooldown.

Follow-up: I’ll add an alternative sku-run with A100 numbers (lower per-GPU perf, need ~1.4x extra slabs).

-Karthik

- Fallback variant: tuned 30B quantized model routed for heavy-tail events to keep p95 < 900ms if needed.
